text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Tuesday morning newspapers:
- A two-day working meeting of NATO members and partner countries started in Brdo, Slovenia, on Monday.
- At the Monday European Union meeting in Brussels, Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler said Slovenia was ready to contribute some policemen to an international police force for Albania.
- Slovenia has not yet decided whether and how to cooperate in the South European Cooperation Initiative (SECI).
- Minister of Economic Affairs Metod Dragonja met the head of Russian gas giant Gazprom in Moscow to discuss the possibility of a Russian gas network running to Italy through Slovenia.
- Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek met former British foreign minister Douglas Hurd, who will participate at the meeting of Slovenian diplomats in Ljubljana.

- In April the refugee status of most of the Bosnian refugees in Slovenia will expire. The government has not yet decided for whom and for how long the status would be prolonged. There are still about 8,000 Bosnian refugees in Slovenia.

- Parliamentary president Janez Podobnik, who visited his U.S. counterpart last week, said high-ranking U.S. officials believed Slovenia fulfils all conditions for being among the first group of countries that will extend NATO.
